_comment: D1/D2: the 29th matrix row, and the ONLY Castalia configuration that exercises the ENABLE_DEBUG RTL arm. D1 gave it the core half of debug -- dcsr/dpc/dscratch0/dscratch1 at 0x7B0-0x7B3 (legal ONLY in debug mode), the DRET encoding, an unmaskable halt request sampled at the fourteen FSM recognition points (the thirteen an interrupt uses PLUS the terminal TRAP_STATE, so a debugger can rescue a wedged hart), the parked-hart clock ungate that makes harts 1..N-1 reachable at all, halt-on-reset, ebreak-to-debug under dcsr.ebreakm, and single-step. D2 ADDS THE OTHER HALF: the assembly-level Debug Module dm0 (always-on mclk, one per chip, a new arbiter MASTER), the eight dmi_* ports on the MCU entity, the per-tile dbg_* hookup with the dbg_halted isolation clamp, and DEBUG_ENTRY_ADDR moved from the TCM default 0xBE00 to the SHARED-WINDOW page 0x00010780 (R-DD3/R-D2-1(3): a tile's TCM is unreachable from the shared bus, so the DM could never place code at 0xBE00). priv is now NAMED rather than inherited (R-D2-2(2), and the CLAUDE.md inheritance-trap discipline): trapCsr because the debug=>trapCsr validator requires it, and umode because the dcsr.prv U-mode instrument needs debug.enable AND priv.umode in one build and no row had both. NOTE what this row still does NOT do in a plain suite run: verify_stage grades a0 from xrun_parallel with no tcl harness, and every debug instrument needs one to force dbg_haltreq or the DMI port -- so the DM is proven by the D-series instruments (xrun_dbg.sh + the dbg_*.tcl harnesses), not by this row's count. Prove with: SUITE=full make verify CONFIG=config/castalia_debug.json
